instruction: In the open spreadsheet, add a SUM formula in cell A21 to calculate the total of all numeric values in column A.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent attempted to change decimal separator from dot to comma. Navigated to Tools > Options > Language Settings, changed locale to French (France), opened Format Cells dialog, then tried a Python script approach which failed with syntax errors. Ran out of 50 turns.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate LibreOffice Calc menus, open Tools > Options, change language/locale settings, select cell ranges, open Format Cells dialog, type in cells
metadata.failure_analysis: Model changed locale display but failed to actually modify cell values. Python script approach had syntax errors and the model could not recover within the turn limit.
metadata.task_rationale: Simplified to a single formula entry task (SUM) which is within the model's demonstrated ability to interact with cells in LibreOffice Calc
metadata.explanation: Task requires entering a SUM formula in cell A21. Getter reads the cell value from the saved xlsx file. Metric checks if the value equals 19.0 (sum of 0.1 to 1.9) with tolerance of 0.1.

scoring_breakdown.sum_formula: 1.0 - Cell A21 contains correct SUM value (~19.0)

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads cell A21 from sheet 0 of the target xlsx file using data_only=True to get calculated values
Postconfig properly saves the file (Ctrl+S) before getter reads, ensuring cached formula values are fresh
Metric correctly handles expected parameter for type='rule' - directly accesses expected.get('expected_value') and expected.get('tolerance')
Expected value of 19.0 is mathematically correct: sum of arithmetic sequence 0.1+0.2+...+1.9 = 19*(0.1+1.9)/2 = 19.0
Tolerance of 0.1 is reasonable for floating-point arithmetic

Minor gap: evaluator verifies the resulting value but does not verify that a SUM formula was specifically used (agent could type =19 directly). This is standard practice but slightly under-verifies the instruction.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Optionally add a second check that reads the cell formula (not data_only) to verify it contains '=SUM(' to fully verify the instruction requirement of using a SUM formula
